ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Cleopatra Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: First prenatal visit at 9 weeks: the uterus is larger than dates; prenatal tests and an early ultrasound with maternal-fetal medicine. Concerns: At nine weeks her belly already looks bigger than it did at the same stage with her son, and the nausea is worse; she wants to know why; She wants to keep working as long as it is safe; Her partner is often away, and she wants a plan for appointments and the birth that she can manage with her household. [S]

Two tablets at bedtime; may add one in the morning if needed

One tablet by mouth at bedtime from 12 weeks until delivery

tr.td: First-trimester ultrasound at 11 weeks with nuchal translucency: two live intrauterine fetuses; a thick dividing membrane with a twin-peak (lambda) sign at a fused anterior placental mass (dichorionic diamniotic); crown-rump lengths 45 and 46 mm; nuchal translucency 1.6 and 1.8 mm; nasal bones present; no structural abnormality seen; no fibroids; no features of a molar pregnancy

Detailed anatomy ultrasound of both twins at 19 weeks: normal anatomy in each; dividing membrane confirmed; fused anterior placenta clear of the cervix; normal amniotic fluid around each twin; transvaginal cervical length 41 mm
Transvaginal measurement of cervical length at 22 weeks: 39 mm, closed internal os, no funneling
Growth ultrasound at 25 weeks: estimated weights 760 g (twin A) and 720 g (twin B), discordance 5 percent; normal amniotic fluid in each sac; normal umbilical artery Doppler
Growth ultrasound at 33 weeks: estimated weights 2050 g (twin A, cephalic) and 1890 g (twin B, breech), discordance 8 percent; normal amniotic fluid in each sac; normal umbilical artery Doppler

tr.td: First prenatal visit at 9 weeks: the uterus is larger than dates; prenatal tests and an early ultrasound with maternal-fetal medicine
Prenatal visit at 11 weeks with the maternal-fetal medicine consultation and first-trimester ultrasound
Prenatal visit at 19 weeks with the detailed anatomy scans and cervical length
Same-day sick visit for vomiting, diarrhea, and tightenings at 22 weeks
Prenatal visit at 25 weeks: growth scan, glucose challenge, and blood count
Prenatal visit at 33 weeks: growth scan, Tdap, and the delivery plan

First prenatal visit: blood count, ferritin, quantitative hCG, blood group and antibody screen, rubella immunity, hepatitis B surface antigen, HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis C tests; urine culture; influenza vaccine; prenatal vitamin with folic acid

Maternal-fetal medicine consultation with a first-trimester ultrasound at 11 weeks for a uterus large for dates: dating, the number of fetuses and, if more than one, chorionicity; nuchal translucency; and fibroids or a molar pregnancy
Nausea and vomiting: small, frequent, bland meals, ginger, and doxylamine with pyridoxine at bedtime; return for vomiting that stops her keeping fluids down, weight loss, or dizziness
Iron deficiency anemia: ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day; blood count and ferritin at the anatomy-scan visit, with intravenous iron in the second trimester if there is no response
Mood: EPDS in each trimester and after the birth

Twin pregnancy care (dichorionic diamniotic): aneuploidy screening by nuchal translucency for each fetus and cell-free DNA, with chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis available; detailed anatomy scans at 18 to 22 weeks; growth scans every four weeks from 20 weeks with discordance calculated; prenatal visits every two to four weeks; weight gain of about 17 to 25 kg; weekly fetal testing may be considered from 36 weeks
Preeclampsia prevention: aspirin 81 mg at bedtime from 12 weeks until delivery, because a twin pregnancy is a high-risk factor; blood pressure and urine protein at every visit

Preterm birth: teaching on the signs of preterm labor; cervical length at the anatomy scan; no cerclage, pessary, progesterone, or bed rest for a twin pregnancy alone; antenatal corticosteroids if birth before 34 weeks is threatened
Gestational diabetes: one-hour glucose challenge at 24 to 28 weeks

Delivery plan: birth at 38 0/7 to 38 6/7 weeks in a hospital with a neonatal intensive care unit; vaginal birth while twin A is head down, with an epidural and the operating room ready for twin B; active management of the third stage for the higher risk of hemorrhage; group B streptococcus swab at 36 to 37 weeks; RSV vaccine at 32 to 36 weeks once the season begins in September; Tdap at 27 to 36 weeks
The cause of the large uterus and the dating of the pregnancy established at the 11-week scan
Dichorionic diamniotic twins; dating by her last period confirmed by the crown-rump lengths
An informed choice about aneuploidy screening by 14 weeks
Chose nuchal translucency for each twin with cell-free DNA; declined diagnostic testing for now
Hemoglobin and ferritin in the normal range for pregnancy by the third trimester
Ferritin 31 ng/mL at 25 weeks; hemoglobin 11.0 g/dL at 33 weeks
Growth discordance under 20 percent at every growth scan
Discordance 5 percent at 25 weeks and 8 percent at 33 weeks
A written delivery plan agreed by 34 weeks
Planned birth at 38 weeks 0 days in the hospital, with a vaginal birth while twin A is head down, an epidural, and the operating room ready
